reference.title: Band Single Arm Shoulder Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the shoulder, breathe out as you press against the band; breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; choke up on the band under the foot, for more tension.
prescription.progression: More reps, a slower return, a shorter band length under the foot (more stretch), then the next band up.

cues.text: Staggered stance: right foot forward standing on the band, left foot back, knees soft, ribs down and glutes lightly braced. Handle at the right shoulder, palm forward, elbow under the wrist; left hand on the hip.
Breathe out and press straight up against the band; do not lean away from it.
Arm nearly straight overhead, biceps near the ear, ribs down; the band is tightest here.
Lower in about 2 s to shoulder height, elbow under the wrist; do not let the band pull the arm down.
Brace again and repeat; switch arms (and the front foot) after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning sideways or back as the band gets tight at the top
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and brace the obliques; use a lighter band.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to finish
mistakes.fix: Ribs down, glutes tight; stop just short of lockout if needed.
Keep the elbow a little in front of the shoulder (scapular plane).

mistakes.mistake: Band slipping from under the foot
mistakes.fix: Keep the band under the middle of the front foot with the foot flat.

kinematics.norm: From about 80-90 degrees (upper arm about level) to about 160-170 degrees overhead (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the bottom with the forearm vertical, nearly straight at the top (clinical opinion)
Elbow about 20-40 degrees in front of the frontal plane (scapular plane; clinical opinion)
Upright with no side lean over a staggered stance; unilateral standing presses increase oblique demand (Saeterbakken 2012)
Under the front foot, so tension rises as the hand goes up and is highest overhead; elastic resistance can give muscle activity comparable to free weights in shoulder exercises (Andersen 2010)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band Single Arm Shoulder Press, video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjørnlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a heavy bench frame or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is lightest at the start and heaviest at the end of the push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder pain overhead: press with the palm facing in (neutral grip) and the elbow further forward.
Low-back discomfort: press half-kneeling with the band under the front knee's foot.
progressions: Stronger band or a shorter band length.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover. The shoulder press gave the highest anterior deltoid activity of four upper-body exercises (Campos 2020); standing presses gave more deltoid activity than seated with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main mover. The shoulder press gave the highest anterior deltoid activity of four upper-body exercises (Campos 2020); standing presses gave more deltoid activity than seated with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lifts the arm up and out; medial deltoid activity in the press was close to the lateral raise (Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Lifts the arm up and out; medial deltoid activity in the press was close to the lateral raise (Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow in the top half.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbow in the top half.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade overhead.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade so the arm can reach fully overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade so the arm can reach fully overhead.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist side-bending toward the band. Unilateral standing presses raised external oblique activity well above bilateral presses (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist side-bending toward the band. Unilateral standing presses raised external oblique activity well above bilateral presses (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down and the trunk stacked over the pelvis; standing presses used far more abdominal activity than seated (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the spine tall; erector spinae activity was higher in the unilateral standing press (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the spine tall; erector spinae activity was higher in the unilateral standing press (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the ball of the shoulder as the arm rises.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the ball of the shoulder as the arm rises.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level against the one-sided load over the staggered stance.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level against the one-sided load over the staggered stance.
